primary_source.directly_read: The complete Height process proposition (prop:height) and proof, including the entire [0,1] uniform topology, common Brownian endpoint, and negligible tau=0 case.

independent_checks: The all-time-minimum prefix contains distinct states, so the finite correction is bounded by one third of the harmonic sum through the prefix length; no future parity renewal is assumed.

For every deterministic divergent w_X=o(sqrt(log X)), the clock lies before tau with probability tending to one and its ratio to tau tends to one. Uniform topology and continuity justify the random evaluation.
The constants satisfy 2c_*/(log3 sqrt(mu))=1, giving the claimed standard normal odd-count scaling.

The all-clock full-law TV estimate transfers the ordinary CDF uniformly to the actual same-path stationary selector after division by its exact mass X/2^h. The result is relative at that rare-event scale.
At fixed critical u, the survivor event converges jointly to {Z>u}; the grade observation converges to the same Z there, giving exactly (Phi(t)-Phi(u))_+.
The fixed-window extension retains the exact sqrt(h/(mu log X)) coefficient for uniform nonperiodic exclusion at t<u. The distinct-orbit product bounds exclude all escaping and pre-entry sources.
On each entered cycle G=u+r_C(Z-u)+o_P(1); the threshold is below the entry boundary. Proper minimum-law tightness justifies summing the countable cyclic component mixture.
The nonstandard-cycle coefficient r_*<1 gives a strictly positive deficit from the Gaussian coefficient, and positive predecessors are used only for the universal-convergence upgrade.
scope_limits: The median closing lower bound is not established.
The moving precritical convergence has no uniform convergence rate over choices of w_X.
Uniform CDF convergence does not imply relative Gaussian-tail estimates for growing thresholds.
The analytic external development is a named written input, not freshly Lean rebuilt here.
